stories.hook: ¿Por qué la ketamina domina los ensayos de depresión resistente?
stories.headline: Ketamina y esketamina lideran la investigación clínica en depresión resistente
stories.finding: De 363 ensayos entre 2014‑2024, la mayoría se enfocó en anestesia (~22 %) y dolor (~28 %) para ketamina, mientras que la depresión resistente representó ≈29 % de los estudios de esketamina. Los ensayos de depresión resistente ya alcanzan fase III/IV y suelen combinarse con electroconvulsiva, psicoterapia, realidad virtual o estimulación magnética transcraneal.
stories.takeaway: Este amplio cuerpo de ensayos evidencia la consolidación de ketamina/esketamina como tratamientos de primera línea para la depresión resistente y su integración con otras intervenciones, orientando decisiones clínicas y futuras investigaciones.
stories.paperTitle: Ketamine and Esketamine in Clinical Trials: FDA‐ Approved and Emerging Indications, Trial Trends With Putative Mechanistic Explanations
stories.originalAbstract: Ketamine has a long and very eventful pharmacological history. Its enantiomer, esketamine ((S)-ketamine), was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and EMA for patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD) in 2019. The number of approved indications for ketamine and esketamine continues to increase, as well as the number of clinical trials. This analysis provides a quantitative overview of the use of ketamine and its enantiomers in clinical trials during 2014-2024. A total of 363 trials were manually assessed from clinicaltrial.gov with the search term "Ketamine." The highest number of trials were found for the FDA-approved indications: anesthesia (~22%) and pain management (~28%) for ketamine and TRD for esketamine (~29%). Clinical trials on TRD for both ketamine and esketamine also comprised a large proportion of these trials, and interestingly, have reached phase III and phase IV status. Combinatorial treatment of psychiatric disorders and non-psychiatric conditions with pharmacological and non-pharmacological combinations (electroconvulsive therapy, psychotherapeutic techniques, virtual reality, and transcranial magnetic stimulation) is prevalent. Sub-anesthetic doses of ketamine may represent novel therapeutic avenues in neuropsychiatric conditions, that is, major depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder, where glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative stress are likely to be involved. The study suggests that the number of ketamine studies will continue to grow and possible ketamine variants can be approved for treatment of additional indications.

stories.headline: La fusión cognitiva medía la relación entre creencias metacognitivas y la rumiación
stories.finding: En una muestra de 149 adultos, el análisis de mediación mostró que la fusión cognitiva mediaba significativamente la relación entre las creencias metacognitivas sobre la incontrolabilidad de la preocupación y la intensidad del worry; la aceptación tuvo un efecto mediador mucho más débil.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir sobre la fusión cognitiva podría reducir la rumiación más eficazmente que enfocarse solo en la aceptación, orientando nuevas estrategias terapéuticas en MCT y ACT.
stories.paperTitle: Metabeliefs about worry, cognitive fusion, and acceptance: associations and mediations analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Although metacognitive therapy (MCT) and acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) are grounded in different theoretical frameworks, both target repetitive negative thinking (RNT) processes, such as worry and rumination, and share a focus on fostering psychological flexibility and reducing experiential avoidance. However, no integrated theoretical model currently exists to combine their potential strengths. Recent research highlights the importance of metacognitive beliefs and acceptance-related processes in maintaining maladaptive RNT. Objective: This study aimed to explore metacognitive and acceptance-based variables in relation to RNT. Methods: The sample consisted of 149 people (116 females), aged between 18 and 71 (M = 34.7; SD = 14.9) who answered the following questionnaires: PSWQ, The AAQ-II, The CFQ, The VQ, MCQ-30 and TCQ. Results: The mediation analysis reveals that cognitive fusion significantly mediated the relationship between metacognitive beliefs and worry, whereas acceptance had a weaker mediating effect. Conclusion: Beliefs about the uncontrollability of worry appear to play a pivotal role in sustaining worry, primarily through their influence on cognitive fusion. These findings provide preliminary support for conceptual overlaps between MCT and ACT in addressing RNT. However, as this is an exploratory and cross-sectional study, conclusions about treatment mechanisms should be drawn cautiously, and future longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to strengthen these insights.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la respiración alta sustituir a los psicodélicos?
stories.headline: La respiración de alta ventilación induce estados similares a psicodélicos
stories.finding: En un estudio exploratorio, 48 profesionales de salud mental participaron en un taller de respiración de alta ventilación (HVB) y reportaron estados alterados de conciencia con intensidad comparable a dosis moderadas de psicodélicos serotonérgicos. Los análisis t mostraron que el potencial clínico percibido superó significativamente los riesgos anticipados.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la HVB podría ofrecer una alternativa no farmacológica para inducir experiencias terapéuticas similares a las de los psicodélicos, ampliando opciones de intervención para trastornos internalizantes sin los retos regulatorios de los fármacos psicodélicos.
stories.paperTitle: High ventilation breathwork as a non-pharmacological model for inducing psychedelic-like states: expert evaluations of therapeutic potential and risk
stories.originalAbstract: High ventilation breathwork (HVB) can induce altered states of consciousness with phenomenological similarities to those reported following administration of serotonergic psychedelics such as lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), psilocybin or ayahuasca. Non-pharmacological methods capable of reliably eliciting such states may provide scalable models for investigating therapeutic mechanisms associated with psychedelic experiences while avoiding pharmacological and regulatory constraints. However, the therapeutic relevance and risk-benefit profile of HVB remain insufficiently characterized. In this exploratory study, 48 mental health professionals participated in an HVB workshop and evaluated perceived therapeutic potential, risks, and potential clinical indications. Participants reported altered states reaching intensity ranges comparable to those described in studies using moderate doses of serotonergic psychedelics. Internalizing disorders were suggested as indications, whereas psychotic, dissociative, and bipolar disorders were identified as contraindications. T-tests showed that perceived clinical potential of HVB significantly outweighed anticipated risks. Exploratory regression analyses indicated that trait openness and emotional breakthrough predicted perceived potential of HVB. HVB may represent a feasible non-pharmacological psychedelic induction paradigm warranting evaluation in controlled clinical trials.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la TCC revertir la activación cerebral alterada en ansiedad infantil?
stories.headline: La TCC normaliza la activación fronto-parietal en niños ansiosos
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado, 69 jóvenes con trastorno de ansiedad recibieron 12 semanas de TCC y redujeron la hiperactivación fronto-parietal durante una tarea de amenaza, alcanzando niveles similares a los 62 controles sanos. Esta normalización se confirmó en análisis de activación regional y en comparaciones longitudinales.
stories.takeaway: Demuestra que la TCC no solo alivia síntomas, sino que también modula circuitos neuronales implicados en la amenaza, lo que sugiere un mecanismo neurobiológico subyacente y apoya su uso temprano en poblaciones pediátricas.
stories.paperTitle: Normalization of Fronto-Parietal Activation by Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy in Unmedicated Pediatric Patients With Anxiety Disorders
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: Anxiety disorders are prevalent among youths and are often highly impairing. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is an effective first-line treatment. The authors investigated the brain mechanisms associated with symptom change following CBT. METHODS: Unmedicated youths diagnosed with an anxiety disorder underwent 12 weeks of CBT as part of two randomized clinical trials testing the efficacy of adjunctive computerized cognitive training. Across both trials, participants completed a threat-processing task during functional MRI before and after treatment. Age-matched healthy comparison youths completed two scans over the same time span. The mean age of the samples was 13.20 years (SD=2.68); 41% were male (youths with anxiety disorders, N=69; healthy comparison youths, N=62). An additional sample including youths at temperamental risk for anxiety (N=87; mean age, 10.51 years [SD=0.43]; 41% male) was utilized to test the stability of anxiety-related neural differences in the absence of treatment. Whole-brain regional activation changes (thresholded at p<0.001) were examined using task-based blood-oxygen-level-dependent response. RESULTS: Before treatment, patients with an anxiety disorder exhibited altered activation in fronto-parietal attention networks and limbic regions relative to healthy comparison children across all task conditions. Fronto-parietal hyperactivation normalized over the course of treatment, whereas limbic responses remained elevated after treatment. In the at-risk sample, overlapping clusters emerged between regions showing stable associations with anxiety over time and regions showing treatment-related changes. CONCLUSIONS: Activation in fronto-parietal networks may normalize after CBT in unmedicated pediatric anxiety patients. Limbic regions may be less amenable to acute CBT effects. Findings from the at-risk sample suggest that treatment-related changes may not be attributed solely to the passage of time.

stories.headline: Terapia asistida con psicodélicos muestra potencial para el PTSD
stories.finding: Los ensayos clínicos iniciales indican que la terapia asistida con psicodélicos puede reducir los síntomas del trastorno de estrés postraumático, ofreciendo una alternativa a los tratamientos tradicionales que dejan a muchos pacientes sintomáticos. El artículo revisa la evidencia emergente y destaca la necesidad de más estudios controlados.
stories.takeaway: Este dato sugiere una vía innovadora que podría ampliar las opciones terapéuticas para pacientes con PTSD resistente, impulsando investigaciones y potencialmente transformando la práctica clínica.
stories.paperTitle: The Psychedelic Future of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Treatment
stories.originalAbstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a mental health condition that can occur following exposure to a traumatic experience. An estimated 12 million U.S. adults are presently affected by this disorder. Current treatments include psychological therapies (e.g., exposure-based interventions) and pharmacological treatments (e.g., selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)). However, a significant proportion of patients receiving standard-of-care therapies for PTSD remain symptomatic, and new approaches for this and other trauma-related mental health conditions are greatly needed. Psychedelic compounds that alter cognition, perception, and mood are currently being examined for their efficacy in treating PTSD despite their current status as Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)- scheduled substances. Initial clinical trials have demonstrated the potential value of psychedelicassisted therapy to treat PTSD and other psychiatric disorders. In this comprehensive review, we summarize the state of the science of PTSD clinical care, including current treatments and their shortcomings. We review clinical studies of psychedelic interventions to treat PTSD, trauma-related disorders, and common comorbidities. The classic psychedelics psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), and N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) and DMT-containing ayahuasca, as well as the entactogen 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) and the dissociative anesthetic ketamine, are reviewed. For each drug, we present the history of use, psychological and somatic effects, pharmacology, and safety profile. The rationale and proposed mechanisms for use in treating PTSD and traumarelated disorders are discussed. This review concludes with an in-depth consideration of future directions for the psychiatric applications of psychedelics to maximize therapeutic benefit and minimize risk in individuals and communities impacted by trauma-related conditions.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el idioma transformar la alianza terapéutica?
stories.headline: El uso del idioma como puente y barrera en terapia bilingüe: estudio de caso
stories.finding: En diez sesiones (14 semanas, con cuatro cancelaciones) con una estudiante china, el idioma bilingüe sirvió como puente que facilitó la comprensión y como barrera que generó malentendidos. El análisis con la Técnica de Incidentes Críticos reveló que estos momentos lingüísticos afectaron la alianza terapéutica y la regulación emocional.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a los terapeutas bilingües sobre el doble papel del idioma, sugiriendo que la atención deliberada a los incidentes lingüísticos puede optimizar la alianza y la regulación emocional, mejorando la eficacia de la intervención.
stories.paperTitle: Language Use as Both Bridge and Barrier in Bilingual Therapy: A Single Case Study Analysis of the Chinese International College Student, “Mary”
stories.originalAbstract: Psychologists often encounter clients from varied language and cultural backgrounds, which can pose challenges to the process of helping. The case of "Mary," an unmarried, 24-year-old Chinese international student in the U.S., embodies these dynamics and offers insights into how culture and language shape, and are shaped by, the therapy alliance, process, and outcome in bilingual therapy. Mary was seen in individual therapy that combined a multicultural, relational psychodynamic, humanistic, client-centered, and solution-focused approach by one of the authors (Y.X.) for 10 sessions (over a 14-week period, with four cancellations); and the therapy was supervised by the other author (J.N.F.). Mary’s presenting problems included challenges in adjusting to her new environment, including a decline in self-confidence and difficulties in her social life, which led to significant anxiety in her daily life. To enhance understanding of the course of therapy, we employed an adapted version of the Critical Incidents Technique (CIT) to analyze significant moments in Mary’s 10 sessions. We focus on the role of language use in bilingual therapy, exploring its functionality as both (a) a buffer against the intense impact of emotional and traumatic experiences, and (b) as a bridge that can foster deeper psychological engagement. We highlight the mechanisms by which the therapist, with supervision, attempted to provide Mary with a meaningful and helpful psychotherapeutic experience. The core theme in our analysis of the case includes the ways that Mary uses her primary (Mandarin) and secondary (English) languages to avoid, and then access, hurtful and traumatic experiences.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el sueño reducir el comer emocional?
stories.headline: Mejor sueño y mayor resiliencia disminuyen la alimentación emocional mediante menor estrés
stories.finding: En 400 estudiantes, el estrés percibido medió la relación entre calidad del sueño y alimentación emocional (efecto indirecto −0.26; total −0.276). Asimismo, la resiliencia psicológica mostró un efecto indirecto de −0.29 y total de −0.282, subrayando el papel del estrés.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que mejorar la calidad del sueño y fortalecer la resiliencia pueden disminuir la alimentación emocional al reducir el estrés percibido, ofreciendo una vía práctica para intervenciones preventivas en jóvenes universitarios.
stories.paperTitle: The Mediating Role of Perceived Stress in the Relationship Between Sleep Quality and Psychological Resilience with Emotional Eating in Students
stories.originalAbstract: The present study aimed to determine the mediating role of perceived stress in the relationship between sleep quality and psychological resilience with emotional eating in students. The research method was descriptive–correlational. The statistical population included all students of the Islamic Azad University, Rasht Branch, during the 2024–2025 academic year. A sample of 400 participants was selected through convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Salzburg Emotional Eating Scale (Meule et al., 2018), the Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (Connor & Davidson, 2003), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (Buysse et al., 1989), and the Perceived Stress Scale (Cohen, 1983). The results showed that the indirect effect of sleep quality on emotional eating was −0.26, and the total effect of sleep quality on emotional eating was −0.276. Moreover, the indirect effect of psychological resilience on emotional eating was −0.29, while the total effect of psychological resilience on emotional eating was estimated at −0.282. The model also demonstrated a good fit. The findings highlight the importance of enhancing psychological resilience and improving sleep quality as effective strategies to reduce unhealthy behaviors such as emotional eating among students.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influye el sueño en la adicción a los videojuegos?
stories.headline: El sueño media la relación entre IGD, TDAH y trastornos emocionales
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática de 17 estudios (2020‑2025) encontró una asociación positiva entre trastorno de juego por internet‑TDAH y depresión, ansiedad y sueño. El sueño actúa como mediador parcial, pues tanto el TDAH como el IGD alteran el ritmo circadiano y la calidad del sueño, reforzando el ciclo patológico.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir en la calidad y regularidad del sueño podría romper la espiral entre el juego excesivo, el TDAH y los síntomas emocionales, ofreciendo una vía terapéutica accesible para adolescentes.
stories.paperTitle: Unraveling the Internet Gaming Disorder and ADHD Link in Adolescents: The Role of Depression, Anxiety, and Sleep
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are two emerging mental health problem that is found to be associated. This comorbiditiy is shared by features such as impulsivity, inattention, and impaired self-regulation. However, the role of comorbid depression, anxiety, and sleep in this relationship remains underexplored. Methods: We conducted a systematic review in accordance to PRISMA guidelines, searching ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2020-2025. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are checked before manual abstract and full-text screening are performed. Risk of Bias (RoB) are assessed by JBI’s checklist. A total of 17 studies were included. Results: Findings consistently revealed a positive association between IGD-ADHD and depression, anxiety, sleep. Depression and anxiety commonly mediate this relationship, with adolescents using gaming as an escape from emotional distress, which in turn worsened executive dysfunction and emotional regulation. Sleep are also identified as partial mediators, as both ADHD and IGD disrupt circadian rhythm and sleep quality, reinforcing the cycle. Conclusions: The link between ADHD and IGD in adolescents is robust and influenced by depression, anxiety, and sleep. These factors act as mediators and amplifiers in a bidirectional pathway, highlighting the need for integrative prevention and intervention strategies that address both behavioral regulation and emotional well-being.

stories.hook: ¿Qué proceso impulsa la mejora del dolor crónico?
stories.headline: La autocompasión y aceptación reducen dolor crónico más que la TCC
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 61 pacientes en MSC y 59 en TCC, la MSC generó aumentos mayores en aceptación del dolor y reducciones más pronunciadas de la sensación de indefensión. Estos cambios explicaron mejoras en autocompasión, depresión, calidad de vida mental e interferencia del dolor.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que potenciar la aceptación y la autocompasión puede ser clave para optimizar tratamientos de dolor crónico, orientando a los clínicos a preferir intervenciones basadas en mindfulness cuando se busca reducir la interferencia del dolor y mejorar el bienestar emocional.
stories.paperTitle: Shared and Differential Psychological Processes Associated With Treatment Response in Mindful Self‐Compassion and Cognitive‐Behavioural Therapy for Chronic Pain: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological treatments for chronic pain are effective, but the processes associated with therapeutic change, and whether these are shared across treatments or treatment-specific, remain unclear. This exploratory secondary analysis examined whether changes in pain acceptance, pain catastrophizing facets and self-compassion were associated with clinical outcomes in Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) versus Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT). METHODS: Data were drawn from a randomized trial comparing MSC (n = 61) and CBT (n = 59) in adults with chronic pain and elevated emotional distress. Processes and outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-treatment. Single and theoretically ordered multiple-mediator models examined whether changes in pain acceptance, rumination, magnification, helplessness and self-compassion were associated with changes in anxiety, depression, quality of life, pain interference and pain intensity. RESULTS: Compared with CBT, MSC produced larger increases in pain acceptance and reductions in helplessness. These processes statistically accounted for improvements in self-compassion, depression, mental quality of life and pain interference; acceptance additionally accounted for reduced pain intensity, and helplessness for reduced anxiety. Rumination and magnification predicted improvements across treatments but did not explain between-group differences. Multiple-mediator models indicated that acceptance/self-compassion and helplessness/self-compassion pathways favoured MSC for depression, anxiety and mental quality of life, explaining up to 51% of change. No mediator accounted for physical quality of life. CONCLUSIONS: MSC and CBT appeared to engage overlapping processes, with differential associations mainly involving pain acceptance and helplessness. Acceptance may be more relevant to functional and pain-related outcomes, whereas helplessness/self-compassion pathways may be more relevant to emotional recovery. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies pain acceptance and reduced helplessness as candidate processes associated with treatment response in MSC and CBT, with acceptance more closely linked to pain-related and functional change and helplessness to emotional outcomes. These findings support more precise, process-based psychological treatment for chronic pain.
stories.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological treatments for chronic pain are effective, but the processes associated with therapeutic change, and whether these are shared across treatments or treatment-specific, remain unclear. This exploratory secondary analysis examined whether changes in pain acceptance, pain catastrophizing facets and self-compassion were associated with clinical outcomes in Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) versus Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT). METHODS: Data were drawn from a randomized trial comparing MSC (n = 61) and CBT (n = 59) in adults with chronic pain and elevated emotional distress. Processes and outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-treatment. Single and theoretically ordered multiple-mediator models examined whether changes in pain acceptance, rumination, magnification, helplessness and self-compassion were associated with changes in anxiety, depression, quality of life, pain interference and pain intensity. RESULTS: Compared with CBT, MSC produced larger increases in pain acceptance and reductions in helplessness. These processes statistically accounted for improvements in self-compassion, depression, mental quality of life and pain interference; acceptance additionally accounted for reduced pain intensity, and helplessness for reduced anxiety. Rumination and magnification predicted improvements across treatments but did not explain between-group differences. Multiple-mediator models indicated that acceptance/self-compassion and helplessness/self-compassion pathways favoured MSC for depression, anxiety and mental quality of life, explaining up to 51% of change. No mediator accounted for physical quality of life. CONCLUSIONS: MSC and CBT appeared to engage overlapping processes, with differential associations mainly involving pain acceptance and helplessness. Acceptance may be more relevant to functional and pain-related outcomes, whereas helplessness/self-compassion pathways may be more relevant to emotional recovery. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies pain acceptance and reduced helplessness as candidate processes associated with treatment response in MSC and CBT, with acceptance more closely linked to pain-related and functional change and helplessness to emotional outcomes. These findings support more precise, process-based psychological treatment for chronic pain.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la ACT mejorar la autoestima en estudiantes de enfermería?
stories.headline: ACT reduce vergüenza internalizada y ansiedad en estudiantes de enfermería
stories.finding: En un estudio cuasi‑experimental con 36 estudiantes de enfermería con fenómeno del impostor, ocho sesiones de ACT de 90 min redujeron significativamente la vergüenza internalizada, el miedo al éxito y la sensibilidad a la ansiedad, según análisis MANCOVA.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la ACT, al fomentar la flexibilidad psicológica, puede ser una herramienta eficaz para fortalecer la autoestima y reducir la autocrítica en futuros profesionales de salud, mejorando su bienestar y desempeño académico.
stories.paperTitle: The Efficacy of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy on Internalized Shame, Fear of Success, and Anxiety Sensitivity in Nursing With Imposter
stories.originalAbstract: The Efficacy of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy on Internalized Shame, Fear of Success, and Anxiety Sensitivity in Nursing With ImposterBackground: Imposter phenomenon (IP), marked by self-doubt and fear of exposure, is common among high-achieving individuals, including nursing students facing academic and clinical pressures.These challenges heighten shame, fear of success, and anxiety sensitivity, harming mental health and performance.Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), focusing on psychological flexibility, is a promising intervention.This study evaluated the ACT's effectiveness in reducing these patterns in nursing students with IP.Methods: This quasi-experimental study used a parallel-group design with pre-test and post-test measures.Thirty-six nursing students with IP from Tehran (Districts 7 and 8) were purposively sampled and non-randomly assigned to the experimental (n=18) and control (n=18) groups.The experimental group attended eight 90-minute ACT sessions, while the control group received no intervention.Data were collected using validated psychological scales and analyzed using MANCOVA, adjusting for baseline scores.Results: The findings revealed that ACT led to a significant reduction in internalized shame (F=39.86,P<0.001), fear of success (F=57.27,P<0.001), and anxiety sensitivity, including its physical (F=56.55,P<0.001), cognitive (F=45.58,P<0.001), and social (F=47.41,P<0.001) dimensions.The effect sizes were large, indicating substantial improvements in the mental health of the experimental group compared to the control group (P<0.001).Conclusion: ACT effectively reduces internalized shame, fear of success, and anxiety sensitivity in nursing students with IP.By fostering psychological flexibility and value-driven behavior, ACT may enhance mental health, academic resilience, and professional confidence.Integrating ACT into nursing education could support students' psychological well-being and success.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el apoyo del supervisor contrarrestar la sobrecarga?
stories.headline: El apoyo del supervisor modera la carga de trabajo y protege el compromiso
stories.finding: En una muestra de 574 técnicos de farmacia, una mayor carga de trabajo cuantitativa se relacionó con menor compromiso laboral (B = −0,290, p < 0,001). El apoyo percibido del supervisor incrementó el compromiso y atenuó la relación negativa entre carga y compromiso (interacción B = 0,156, p = 0,008).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fortalecer el apoyo del supervisor puede mitigar los efectos de la sobrecarga y favorecer el compromiso, ofreciendo una vía práctica para prevenir el burnout en entornos de alta demanda.
stories.paperTitle: Quantitative Workload and Work Engagement Among Community Pharmacy Technicians: The Moderating Role of Perceived Supervisor Support
stories.originalAbstract: Background/Objectives: Research on community pharmacy technicians has rarely examined how workload and supervisor support jointly relate to work engagement. The aim of this study was to examine these relationships among community pharmacy technicians within the Job Demands–Resources framework and to test the moderating role of supervisor support in the workload–work engagement relationship. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 574 community pharmacy technicians recruited from pharmacies selected through stratified random sampling in four provinces of Türkiye. Quantitative workload, perceived supervisor support, and work engagement were measured using validated instruments. Moderation was tested with PROCESS Model 1. Results: When supervisor support was at its mean, higher quantitative workload was associated with lower work engagement (B = −0.290, 95% CI [−0.389, −0.191], p < 0.001). At the mean workload level, supervisor support was positively associated with engagement (B = 0.405, 95% CI [0.295, 0.516], p < 0.001). The interaction between workload and supervisor support was significant but modest in magnitude (B = 0.156, 95% CI [0.041, 0.271], p = 0.008; ΔR2 = 0.010). Simple slopes showed a progressively weaker negative workload–engagement association as supervisor support increased. The interaction remained significant in the covariate-adjusted model (B = 0.148, 95% CI [0.030, 0.266], p = 0.014). Conclusions: Higher quantitative workload was associated with lower work engagement, whereas greater perceived supervisor support was associated with higher engagement. The negative workload–engagement association also weakened as perceived supervisor support increased.

stories.hook: ¿Qué factor impulsa la salud marital por encima de todo?
stories.headline: El amor, más que la comunicación, predice la salud matrimonial
stories.finding: En un estudio transversal con 3,808 adultos estadounidenses, el amor mutuo resultó ser el predictor más fuerte de la salud marital, superando a la comunicación, el respeto, la confianza y la intimidad sexual. Estos resultados resaltan la centralidad del amor en la promoción de matrimonios saludables.
stories.takeaway: Para la práctica clínica, priorizar intervenciones que fortalezcan el vínculo afectivo y el amor entre cónyuges puede ser más eficaz que centrarse únicamente en habilidades comunicativas, ofreciendo una guía basada en evidencia para terapeutas de pareja.
stories.paperTitle: BEYOND SATISFACTION: PREDICTORS AND CORRELATES OF MARITAL HEALTH
stories.originalAbstract: This quantitative, nonexperimental, cross-sectional study evaluated factors associated with and predictive of marital health. Marital health was identified as a more holistic evaluator of marital connection and commitment, moving beyond individual satisfaction. The original sample was taken from the archived Marriage Health in America survey data. The sample included 3,808 United States adults. Participants completed a marital satisfaction index and a marital health measure, while simultaneously ranking 32 identified factors of marital health. The results found that love for each other was the strongest predictor of marital health, followed by communication through listening, respect, trust, and sexual intimacy. These findings underscore the importance of each factor in fostering healthy marriages.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena mejorar la equidad en la calificación?
stories.headline: Mindfulness se vincula a mejor salud mental y satisfacción docente
stories.finding: En una muestra aleatoria estratificada de 1 024 docentes de secundaria en Ghana se evaluaron mindfulness, angustia psicológica, salud mental y percepción de sesgo de calificación mediante cuestionarios validados. Los análisis revelaron que mayores niveles de mindfulness se asociaron positivamente con mejor salud mental y mayor satisfacción laboral.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar la atención plena entre los profesores podría potenciar su bienestar y promover evaluaciones más justas, ofreciendo una vía práctica para mitigar el burnout y el sesgo en contextos educativos.
stories.paperTitle: The Psychology of Fair Assessment: Mindfulness, Mental Health, and Grading Bias Among Senior High School Teachers in Ghana
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: In recent years, teacher well-being and fairness in assessment have emerged as critical issues in higher education, particularly in contexts of rising stress and burnout. This study employed a correlational research design to investigate the relationships among mindfulness, psychological distress, mental health, and assessment fairness among senior high school teachers in Ghana. METHOD: A sample of 1024 teachers from public and private institutions was recruited using stratified random sampling to ensure representation across key demographics. Adopted validated psychometric tools assessed mindfulness (Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire [FFMQ]), psychological distress (Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (10 items) [K10]), mental health status (General Health Questionnaire (12 items) [GHQ-12]), emotional exhaustion (Maslach Burnout Inventory-Emotional Exhaustion subscale [MBI-EE]), job satisfaction survey (JSS), and perceptions of grading bias and fairness. Data were collected via online surveys, enabling wide geographical reach and participant anonymity. RESULT: The results revealed that mindfulness was positively associated with mental health, job satisfaction, and perceptions of assessment fairness, and negatively correlated with psychological distress, emotional exhaustion, and grading bias tendencies. Multiple regression analysis showed that mindfulness (β = 0.30, p < 0.001**), mental health (β = 0.22, p = 0.003**), and job satisfaction (β = 0.25, p = 0.001**) significantly associated assessment fairness perceptions. Conversely, psychological distress (β = -0.24, p = 0.001**), emotional exhaustion (β = -0.21, p = 0.002**), and grading bias tendency (β = -0.27, p = 0.001**) were negative associators. Moderation analysis indicated that mindfulness buffered the detrimental effect of psychological distress on fairness perceptions (interaction β = 0.21, p = 0.003**). Mediation analysis further showed that mental health partially mediated the mindfulness-assessment fairness relationship (indirect β = 0.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] [0.08, 0.21]), suggesting mindfulness fosters fairness perceptions partly by enhancing mental well-being. CONCLUSION: The findings highlight key psychological pathways through which mindfulness supports equitable assessment practices, emphasizing the importance of mindfulness-based interventions and mental health support to promote fairness, reduce bias, and improve teachers' well-being in senior high school education settings.

stories.hook: ¿Los descansos en redes sociales ayudan o perjudican al estudio?
stories.headline: Los descansos en redes sociales pueden favorecer la recuperación o fomentar la procrastinación
stories.finding: El estudio con 20 estudiantes universitarios reveló que factores motivacionales y ambientales, tanto en la fase de inicio como en la de ejecución, determinan si una pausa en redes sociales funciona como recuperación o como procrastinación. Una perspectiva de regulación emocional clarifica las condiciones que favorecen cada resultado.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a docentes y diseñadores de intervenciones a estructurar pausas digitales que potencien la autorregulación emocional, mejorando el bienestar y el rendimiento académico de los estudiantes.
stories.paperTitle: Social Media Breaks: An Opportunity for Recovery and Procrastination
stories.journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
stories.originalAbstract: Social media (SM) breaks from studying can either support students' wellbeing and performance by acting as a recovery behaviour or subvert it by acting as a procrastination behaviour. It is currently unclear which influences lead an SM break to be a positive recovery vs. negative procrastination behaviour. A behavioural and emotion regulation (ER) perspective may help to elucidate these influences. In this paper, we report a semi-structured interview study with 20 undergraduates to explore their experiences of SM breaks when studying. Our analysis describes how motivational and environmental factors can influence a break's propensity for recovery or procrastination during the break initiation and execution phases. We apply an ER perspective to these reports and demonstrate how it helps to explain further in which circumstances SM breaks are likely to support recovery or procrastination. Based on this analysis, we present recommendations for designing interventions to support healthy breaks and reduce unhealthy ones.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la interacción en redes sociales fortalecer la resiliencia durante la pandemia?
stories.headline: El uso activo de redes sociales mantiene capital social y resiliencia colectiva en COVID‑19
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática de 20 estudios encontró que la participación activa en redes sociales mantuvo el capital social y favoreció la resiliencia colectiva durante la pandemia. Además, el apoyo emocional recibido alivió la soledad y facilitó la difusión rápida de información y la movilización comunitaria.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya que fomentar la interacción positiva en redes sociales puede ser una estrategia eficaz para mitigar el aislamiento y fortalecer la resiliencia, ofreciendo a profesionales una herramienta complementaria en intervenciones psicosociales durante crisis sanitarias.
stories.paperTitle: Support from Social Media during the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review
stories.originalAbstract: The social distancing measures in response to the COVID-19 pandemic have transformed people from social to isolated individuals. During that time, social media became a useful tool for satisfying people's need for social interaction. Previous systematic reviews, however, have focused largely on the negative impact of social media use and ignored the positive side. Hence, this systematic review examined the role of social media use in providing support-be it social, emotional or informational-during the pandemic. Four databases were systematically searched, and the selection procedure followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Protocol registration: PROSPERO (CRD42022367903). A total of 20 papers were deemed eligible for data extraction. The findings showed that active engagement on social media contributed significantly to maintaining social capital and collective resilience amidst social restrictions. The emotional support obtained from social media was proven effective in alleviating feelings of loneliness and isolation. Also, social media facilitated the rapid dissemination of information and the grassroots mobilization of support by overcoming bureaucratic hurdles and addressing urgent community needs. This review concluded by highlighting the transformative potential of social media in crisis contexts and suggesting implications for mental health interventions and community resilience strategies.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la conectividad frontal predecir el TDAH temprano?
stories.headline: Mayor conectividad frontoparietal en lactantes con riesgo familiar de TDAH
stories.finding: En 44 infantes (22 de alto riesgo familiar por ADHD) se midió la conectividad funcional con fNIRS a los 8‑10 y 12‑14 meses. Los de alto riesgo mostraron mayores aumentos de conectividad frontoparietal y un desplazamiento izquierdo, asociados a más conductas de ADHD a los 18‑30 meses.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la conectividad frontoparietal temprana puede servir como biomarcador para identificar niños con riesgo de TDAH, facilitando intervenciones preventivas antes de la aparición clínica.
stories.paperTitle: Familial risk for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and related behaviors in toddlerhood are preliminarily associated with altered frontoparietal development in infancy measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood neurodevelopmental disorder associated with impairments across the lifespan. Children with ADHD have been found to have delayed brain maturation. These delays may be present and detectable with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) as early as infancy for children at familial risk for ADHD. The present study examined longitudinal changes in functional connectivity among infants at high and low familial risk for ADHD, and their association with ADHD-related behaviors in toddlerhood. Methods: Participants were 44 infants, half at high familial risk for ADHD due to parental ADHD, assessed at 8-10 months and 12-14 months of age. fNIRS was used to measure hemodynamic activation in frontal and parietal regions during a low cognitive load task of attention. In toddlerhood, 18-30 months of age, parents rated ADHD-related behaviors using the Child Behavior Checklist. Results: Across the sample, longitudinal fNIRS analyses revealed increased frontal connectivity with a notable leftward shift between timepoints. High-risk children showed greater increases in frontoparietal connectivity relative to low-risk peers, with divergent trajectories observed in left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and right parietal connectivity. Greater parent-reported attention symptoms were broadly associated with increased frontoparietal connectivity. Discussion: Although most findings did not survive corrections for multiple comparisons, these findings suggest that familial ADHD risk and early ADHD-related behaviors may be associated with atypical frontoparietal and frontal network development across the first year of life, highlighting the potential of fNIRS as a tool for identifying early neural markers of ADHD risk that could be used to identify which infants could benefit from early preventative interventions.

stories.hook: ¿La dependencia de IA empeora la salud mental adolescente?
stories.headline: Los problemas de salud mental predicen la dependencia de IA en adolescentes, no al revés
stories.finding: El 17,14 % de los adolescentes mostraron dependencia de IA en la primera medición y el 24,19 % en la segunda. Los problemas de salud mental (ansiedad/depresión) predijeron significativamente la dependencia posterior, mientras que la dependencia no anticipó futuros problemas de salud mental.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir en la ansiedad y depresión durante la adolescencia puede prevenir la creciente dependencia de tecnologías de IA, orientando a padres y profesionales a priorizar la salud mental antes que limitar el uso de IA.
stories.paperTitle: AI Technology panic—is AI Dependence Bad for Mental Health? A Cross-Lagged Panel Model and the Mediating Roles of Motivations for AI Use Among Adolescents
stories.originalAbstract: Background: The emergence of new technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), may manifest as technology panic in some people, including adolescents who may be particularly vulnerable to new technologies (the use of AI can lead to AI dependence, which can threaten mental health). While the relationship between AI dependence and mental health is a growing topic, the few existing studies are mainly cross-sectional and use qualitative approaches, failing to find a longitudinal relationship between them. Based on the framework of technology dependence, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of experiencing AI dependence, to examine the cross-lagged effects between mental health problems (anxiety/depression) and AI dependence and to explore the mediating role of AI use motivations. Methods: = 13.21 ± 2.55) was used with a cross-lagged panel model and a half-longitudinal mediation model. Results: 17.14% of the adolescents experienced AI dependence at T1, and 24.19% experienced dependence at T2. Only mental health problems positively predicted subsequent AI dependence, not vice versa. For AI use motivation, escape motivation and social motivation mediated the relationship between mental health problems and AI dependence whereas entertainment motivation and instrumental motivation did not. Discussion: Excessive panic about AI dependence is currently unnecessary, and AI has promising applications in alleviating emotional problems in adolescents. Innovation in AI is rapid, and more research is needed to confirm and evaluate the impact of AI use on adolescents' mental health and the implications and future directions are discussed.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen los astrocitos en trastornos mentales tempranos?
stories.headline: Astrocitos regulan la conectividad sináptica durante períodos críticos y predisponen trastornos mentales
stories.finding: Los astrocitos proliferan, se diferencian y maduran durante el período crítico postnatal, modulando el equilibrio entre formación y eliminación sináptica. Alteraciones en su número, morfología o funciones durante esta ventana pueden producir remodelación sináptica aberrante y desencadenar trastornos neuropsiquiátricos.
stories.takeaway: Comprender el papel de los astrocitos en la plasticidad sináptica temprana abre nuevas vías para intervenciones preventivas y terapéuticas dirigidas a restaurar su función y reducir el riesgo de trastornos mentales en la infancia.
stories.paperTitle: Brain stars take the lead during critical periods of early postnatal brain development: relevance of astrocytes in health and mental disorders
stories.originalAbstract: In the brain, astrocytes regulate shape and functions of the synaptic and vascular compartments through a variety of released factors and membrane-bound proteins. An imbalanced astrocyte activity can therefore have drastic negative impacts on brain development, leading to the onset of severe pathologies. Clinical and pre-clinical studies show alterations in astrocyte cell number, morphology, molecular makeup and astrocyte-dependent processes in different affected brain regions in neurodevelopmental (ND) and neuropsychiatric (NP) disorders. Astrocytes proliferate, differentiate and mature during the critical period of early postnatal brain development, a time window of elevated glia-dependent regulation of a proper balance between synapse formation/elimination, which is pivotal in refining synaptic connectivity. Therefore, any intrinsic and/or extrinsic factors altering these processes during the critical period may result in an aberrant synaptic remodeling and onset of mental disorders. The peculiar bridging position of astrocytes between synaptic and vascular compartments further allows them to "compute" the brain state and consequently secrete factors in the bloodstream, which may serve as diagnostic biomarkers of distinct healthy or disease conditions. Here, we collect recent advancements regarding astrogenesis and astrocyte-mediated regulation of neuronal network remodeling during early postnatal critical periods of brain development, focusing on synapse elimination. We then propose alternative hypotheses for an involvement of aberrancies in these processes in the onset of ND and NP disorders. In light of the well-known differential prevalence of certain brain disorders between males and females, we also discuss putative sex-dependent influences on these neurodevelopmental events. From a translational perspective, understanding age- and sex-dependent astrocyte-specific molecular and functional changes may help to identify biomarkers of distinct cellular (dys)functions in health and disease, favouring the development of diagnostic tools or the selection of tailored treatment options for male/female patients.
